column6: Explainer listed "the early Spider-Man" among pulp heroes; Spider-Man is a 1962 Marvel comics character. Changed to "the Spider" (the 1930s pulp hero).

Old How section labeled Primer as fixed-timeline (its characters repeatedly change events) and All You Need Is Kill as ontological paradox (it is a reset loop). Replaced with Twelve Monkeys [fixed] and Heinlein's "—All You Zombies—" [ontological]; Back to the Future kept.
Checked Sindarin glosses: Mordor "Black Land", Gondor "Stone-land", Moria "Black Chasm", dor "land", mor "black".

Old How section cited Jemisin's Inheritance Trilogy (secondary-world fantasy) and Novik's Scholomance (set in a magic school, not a city) as urban fantasy. Replaced with Jemisin's The City We Became. Explainer still cites Scholomance; left as note.

Old How section called Blood Meridian a canonical western (it is the standard revisionist/anti-western) and called Butler's Parable series and Jemisin's Broken Earth revisionist westerns (they are SF and fantasy). Now: canonical = L'Amour, Wister's The Virginian; revisionist = Blood Meridian, Berger's Little Big Man. Sentence quoted by q:2 explanation kept.
